title: Soft gradients in a recording come out smooth, even where the Mac draws them in steps
goal: Recordings still show visible bands across soft dark gradients, such as a translucent terminal window. The recording now copies the screen exactly, and the screen's own pixels are in steps. Smooth those steps when a recording is PLAYED, shown and EXPORTED, on the GPU, and never while recording: recording itself stays exactly as fast and light as it is today, with no start delay and no dropped frames.
notes:
User, 2026-11-16, after a-screen-recording-keeps-the-desktop-s-colours-a shipped (ce7a9b934, 10-bit HEVC Display P3, captured as kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr10BiPlanarVideoRange in ScreenRecorder.swift:304): "there is no way to fix the visible banding in the recordings? see last recording", with Screenshot 2026-11-16 at 06.33.51.png (the recording playing in Photonz Dev).

Measured by the intake window, G channel down a 1300 px column of the empty sidebar (x 261, y 740..2040): the macOS screenshot of the screen (06.33.18, before the recording) has 11 levels over 53..63, 16 changes, longest flat run 164 px, max step 1. The recording's frame at 3 s, decoded to 16 bit: 8-bit equivalent 11 levels, longest run 161 px; in 10-bit, 28 levels, longest run 116 px, steps of about 3.5 to 4 codes = one 8-bit shade. Colours match within about 1 code. So the recording is now faithful; the SOURCE is drawn in 8-bit steps by the window server (the window's translucent material), and capturing at 10 bit cannot add shades that were never drawn. Whether the user's display hides those steps (panel dithering) is not confirmed; the user sees them as bands in the recording.

ffmpeg deband test on that frame (format=yuv420p10le, deband=1thr=0.004:2thr=0.004:3thr=0.004:range=64:blur=1): 43 levels, longest flat run 35 px. gradfun (8-bit) did not help (10 levels). ffmpeg's CPU deband took 0.6 s wall for 30 frames on 5 cores, far too heavy for 60 fps live, hence the GPU requirement. Smoothing in the player and export instead of at capture keeps recording cheap and the file a faithful copy; smoothing at capture fixes the file for every other player. Measure both. The Smaller files quality setting (Settings > Recording > Quality) must get the same pass.

User, 2026-11-16, on hearing the first version: "that sounds slow? i don't want dropped frames or a start delay". So the pass goes in the display and export path only, never capture. The raw file stays a faithful copy of the screen; other players (QuickTime, Safari) will still show the screen's own steps unless the recording is exported from Photonz. Say that plainly in the audit. A deband on the GPU is a few texture reads a pixel, far below a frame's budget; the CPU timing above was ffmpeg's software filter, not what this will be.
acceptance: Reproduced first on the user's own files: /Users/dzearing/Pictures/Screenshots/Recording 2026-11-16 at 06.33.31.mp4 at 3 s against Screenshot 2026-11-16 at 06.33.18.png, the empty sidebar strip of the Ghoztty window (x 260, y 740 to 2040). Measure what the intake window measured (below) and put it in the audit

A smoothing pass (a deband: where neighbouring areas differ by about one 8-bit shade over a wide flat run, blend them into a smooth 10-bit ramp; leave anything with a real edge alone) runs on the GPU (Metal / Core Image) when a recording is shown in Photonz (player, thumbnails, editor canvas) and when it is exported or copied out. NOTHING in the capture path changes: ScreenRecorder, RecordingFileWriter and the stream settings are untouched, and the diff proves it

Visual bar that today's file FAILS: on that strip the longest flat run is under 40 px and there are at least 35 distinct 10-bit levels (today: 116 px and 28 levels; ffmpeg's deband filter on the same frame reached 35 px and 43 levels, so it can be done). Same bar on a controlled test: a full-screen 8-bit gradient spanning 10 shades over 1300 px

Nothing sharp gets softer: text, window edges, icons and one-pixel lines in the same frames differ from the unsmoothed frame by no more than 1 10-bit code value at the 99th percentile (measured on a text-heavy crop), and colours stay within Delta E 1 of the screenshot

Recording is untouched, MEASURED to prove it: start latency and dropped frames over a minute at 60 fps are identical to before within run-to-run noise (zero new dropped frames). Playback is not slowed either: frame time while playing a 3456x2234 recording at 1x and 2x, scrubbing, and the time to first frame when a recording opens, before and after, with no dropped frames added and no more than 1 ms per frame on the GPU (measured). Export time before and after is listed

Played in QuickTime and in Photonz's player, the before and after crops are put side by side (and a 3x enlarged, contrast-stretched crop so the bands can be seen) under queue/audits/, with a short before/after clip of the user's recording, named in the audit; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

User 2026-11-16: no dropped frames, no start delay. Moved the pass to playback, display and export only; capture path untouched; zero-regression bars on recording and playback.

owns these walks: soft-gradients-in-a-recording-play-smooth-walk

Reproduced on the user's file: frame at 3 s, x 261, y 740-2040, decoded 16-bit: 27 10-bit levels, longest flat 124 px (8-bit 11 levels, 161 px); screenshot 06.33.18: 11 levels, 164 px. Built RecordingSmoothing (PhotonzRender): three Core Image Metal kernels (box shrink by 8, edge-aware 32-tap disc blur, full-size apply with edge/hairline guard and triangular grain). Applied where a recording's frame becomes a picture: MovieSweeper.picture (play/scrub sweeps), MovieDecoder.frame/picture (exact seeks, filmstrip, library poster), DocumentFrames stream frames (drawn export). Capture path untouched. Behind next-soft-gradients-in-a-recording-play-smooth, on by default in Next.

Adversarial pass before building: a deband can soften faint real detail (a 1-shade hairline, a 2 px faint line) and halo near window edges; guarded by leaving any pixel with a neighbour >1.5 shades off, any 1-px line standing off both sides, and any pixel the blur would move by >2.5 shades. Display and export are both 8-bit (canvas RGBA8, export H.264 BGRA), so a smooth ramp alone would be rounded back into the same steps: grain is required, added only where the pass moved a pixel (flat areas come back bit for bit). A Premiere/FCP user never sees a setting for this; it is simply how footage plays. No control added, so no placement question.

Shipped in 1f7993f11 (display slice). On screen, user's recording, sidebar strip, 8 px means: longest flat run 8-26 px, 40 levels (off: 103-137 px). Controlled staircase unit tests pass the bar deep and in 8-bit. Text block on vs off: 0.002% of edge pixels differ, p99 0 codes; colours within 1 10-bit code. GPU +1.0 ms per full 3456 frame (1.4 vs 0.4 ms median, noisy shared Mac), +0.2 ms at half size. Speed walk: 1/1818 missed on and off, scrub lag 2/4 frames both. First sharp frame of a 3456 recording ~1.04 s on and off. Start drill median 8.7 ms (9.6 earlier today). Chose grain (up to a shade, triangular, only where the pass moved a pixel) over handing the canvas 16-bit frames because the canvas and every export round to 8 bits, where a smooth ramp alone falls back into the same steps; rectangular half-shade grain was blended away when the picture is enlarged (fixture at 1.5x: 62 px flat), triangular got 39-41 px.

Chose comparisons in sRGB-curve steps inside the kernels with numbers kept in linear light over matching to the picture's colours and back: the round trip through half floats moved 1 text-edge pixel in 10 by a shade; now 1 in 1000. Tried a 'keep the original pixel' pass too: exact, but 5-7 ms GPU a full frame, dropped.

Chose to smooth drawn exports at High only: at Standard (H.264, 2.2 Mbps for a 1440 wide file) the grain was wiped and the file read 94 px flat vs 95 unsmoothed, in 11.2 s vs 5.4 s. An encoder test at High's ~55 Mbps kept 31 px flat. Copies (High, untouched or cut-only) stay copies of the file: drawing them instead would re-encode 10-bit P3 HEVC as 8-bit sRGB H.264 and take seconds instead of 0.1 s.

LEFT OPEN (why this task stays pending): (1) Exported/copied files for other players are still banded: a High export of an untouched or cut-only recording is the raw file; Standard/Small are unsmoothed. The way through is a 10-bit HEVC drawn export (DocumentMovieWriter writes 8-bit BGRA H.264 today) so the ramp needs no grain, plus deciding whether a High export of a recording draws instead of copying when the pass would change it. (2) No drill counts dropped capture frames over a minute (RecordingFileWriter.frameCounts exists but nothing reads it); capture code is untouched, so only the measurement is missing. (3) GPU bar of 1 ms: +1.0 ms median at full 3456 size, +0.2 at half; borderline at full size on a noisy machine.

Export slice: SmoothedCopyWriter (PhotonzMedia) writes an untouched or cut-only recording out again at its own depth (HEVC Main 10, own colour tags) through the pass with no grain, when ExportSmoothing reads 3 quarter-size frames and the pass moves >=0.2% of a frame's pixels by a 10-bit code; else still copied. Encoder: quality 0.9, spatial adaptive QP off. Chose that over a rate (wrote 9 of 104 Mbps, text p99 19 codes), a quality with a rate cap (quality ignored), AQ on (32 px blocks with 2-3 code jumps, grain kept by chance: 21 px flat at half a shade, 61-70 at 3/4 and 1), and a QP cap (worse). Chose no grain in the file because the encoder drops it unpredictably.

Measured on the user's recording via the probe's High export: 121 MB copied in 0.1 s -> 32.7 MB written in 4.3 s, HEVC Main 10, P3 + sRGB curve kept. Sidebar strip (Apple decoder): 27 -> 38 levels, largest step 4 -> 2 codes, longest flat run 116 -> 68 px (68 is where the gradient bottoms out; the strip spans 31-39 codes over 1300 px, so a grain-free 10-bit ramp averages 33-42 px a code: under 40 px everywhere needs grain, which the encoder drops). Text block: p99 9 codes vs source, identical to a plain re-encode with no filter (9); 3x crops look identical. Standard export 5.2 s (unchanged).
